sentences.text: In the fourth quarter of 2024, the firm performed its annual assessment of goodwill for impairment, for each of its reporting units with goodwill, by performing a qualitative assessment.

• Performance Indicators. During 2024, the firm's net revenues, efficiency ratio (total operating expenses divided by total net revenues), diluted earnings per common share (EPS), return on average common shareholders' equity and book value per common share all improved from 2023 and from 2022 (when a quantitative test was last performed). Within the reporting units with goodwill, there continued to be solid fundamentals underlying our businesses, where the firm continued to maintain industry leadership positions and execute on strategic goals.

• Fair Value Indicators. Fair value indicators for both the firm and its peers have generally improved since the annual assessment performed in 2023 and from 2022 (when a quantitative test was last performed).
During 2024, the Corporation completed its annual goodwill impairment test as of June 30, 2024 using a qualitative assessment for all applicable reporting units.

Based on the assessment, the Corporation has concluded that none of its reporting units are at risk of impairment, as each of the reporting units' fair values are substantially in excess of their carrying values.

comparisons.peer_summary: The goodwill impairment test compares the fair value of each reporting unit with its carrying value, using allocated capital plus goodwill as a proxy for equity carrying values, and determines impairment if fair value is less than carrying value.
comparisons.comparison: Both GS and JPMorgan describe the mechanics of the goodwill impairment test, which compares the fair value of reporting units to their carrying values. A key difference is the metric used for carrying value: JPM explicitly uses 'allocated capital plus goodwill and other intangible assets' as a proxy for equity carrying values, whereas GS's disclosure focuses on the qualitative conclusion of no impairment based on performance and fair value indicators without defining the specific carrying value proxy in this section.

• Fair Value Indicators. Fair value indicators for both the firm and its peers have generally improved since the annual assessment performed in 2023 and from 2022 (when a quantitative test was last performed).
The goodwill impairment test is generally performed by comparing the current fair value of each reporting unit with its carrying value.
If the fair value is in excess of the carrying value, then the reporting unit's goodwill is considered not to be impaired.

comparisons.peer_topic: Goodwill and Indefinite-Lived Intangible Assets Impairment Testing Methodology
comparisons.peer_summary: The Firm tests goodwill and indefinite-lived intangible assets for impairment annually and on an interim basis when events occur. For goodwill, testing is performed at the reporting unit level, while indefinite-lived intangible assets are tested at the aggregate level of management contracts. The Firm may use a qualitative assessment or a quantitative test; if quantitative, impairment is recognized if fair value is less than carrying amount, limited to the asset's carrying amount.
comparisons.comparison: Both GS and Morgan Stanley disclose the methodology for goodwill impairment testing, which includes a qualitative assessment option. GS details the specific qualitative factors considered in its 2024 assessment (performance, events, fair value indicators) to conclude no impairment. MS describes the same structural option to perform a qualitative assessment to determine if it is 'more likely than not' that fair value is less than carrying amount before proceeding to quantitative testing, though MS does not disclose the specific qualitative conclusions for 2024 in this segment, instead noting no impairments were recorded in the recent history.

For both the annual and interim tests, the Firm has the option to either (i) perform a quantitative impairment test or (ii) first perform a qualitative assessment to determine whether it is more likely than not that the fair value is less than its carrying amount, in which case, the quantitative test would be performed.
When performing a quantitative impairment test of goodwill, the Firm compares the fair value of the reporting unit with the carrying amount.
